CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports that she has been struggling with depression more recently due to prolonged isolation and remote work over the past year, with symptoms occurring off and on. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily and reports compliance with this medication. She notes that the medication has helped her in the past and is interested in increasing the dose to help her through the current difficult period.

She also reports ongoing chronic back pain that she has been managing. Pain is worse with prolonged sitting at her desk at work and improves with movement. She describes the back as getting stiff and painful with extended sitting periods. She endorses some numbing sensation but denies tingling or pain radiating down her legs. She notes that symptoms improve when she stands up or changes position. She denies leg weakness. She is able to perform activities of daily living but reports being bothered by extremes of prolonged sitting or standing.

She has a history of congenital coronary artery for which she underwent coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports that her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Depression as noted above. Denies leg pain or tingling. Denies leg weakness. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Congenital coronary artery disease status post coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at a desk job. Recently has been working remotely.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears comfortable, no distress
HEENT: Neck without thyroid enlargement
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased back flexion
Extremities: Lower extremity strength good, no edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable compared to last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Patient agreeable to dose increase. Prescription sent to pharmacy.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy for management of symptoms. Patient prefers physical therapy over pain medication at this time. Physical therapy referral placed.
3. Status post coronary artery bypass grafting: Order echocardiogram for follow-up. Continue aspirin 81 mg daily. Patient agreeable to plan.
